CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for reassessment of anxiety management, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, headache symptoms, and medication review.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a modest improvement in his symptoms since the last visit. He has increased his sertraline dosage to 200 mg daily as discussed, and while he acknowledges some alleviation of anxiety symptoms, he continues to experience significant anxiety episodes, particularly in high-pressure work situations, occurring approximately 3-4 times per week.
Sleep quality has shown slight improvement, with Mr. Smith now averaging 5-6 hours of sleep per night. He reports that the melatonin regimen remains unchanged at 5 mg at bedtime, and he has been more diligent in applying cognitive-behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) techniques, finding them somewhat more helpful in managing his sleep disturbances.
Headaches persist at a frequency of 3 times per week, with intensity remaining moderate to severe. Mr. Smith reports utilizing ibuprofen 400 mg approximately twice weekly for relief, noting that while it provides some relief, he still experiences discomfort. He has started the increased dose of amitriptyline at 10 mg nightly, which he believes may be contributing to a slight reduction in headache frequency, although he has not yet fully assessed its effectiveness.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Melatonin 5 mg at bedtime 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 4. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief 5. Amitriptyline 10 mg nightly
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer and reports that while project demands remain high, he has been employing stress management techniques more effectively. He maintains a walking routine three times a week and has recommitted to mindfulness meditation, which he finds beneficial during particularly stressful periods. He remains abstinent from alcohol and is focused on enhancing his overall well-being.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Notable reduction in anxiety frequency; persistent sleep disturbances; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Ongoing tension-type headaches as previously described; no visual changes or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue noted; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 122/78 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert and oriented, in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears moderately anxious, with some improvement noted.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Discuss the potential for a trial of lorazepam as needed for acute anxiety episodes, particularly during peak work stress. 2. Insomnia: Continue melatonin at 5 mg at bedtime; reinforce CBT-I strategies. Monitor sleep patterns closely and consider a sleep study if no further improvement is noted. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue ibuprofen as needed; assess the efficacy of amitriptyline at 10 mg nightly and consider further adjustments if headache frequency does not improve. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Continue to encourage physical activity and mindfulness practices; consider referral to a nutritionist for dietary optimization to support energy levels.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2027-07-01 to evaluate ongoing symptoms, assess treatment effectiveness, and discuss further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any worsening of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
